headline: Majors above 200s with RSI in the 70s and funding elevated, but ETF flows and whale movements show conflicting signals within the same windows
paragraphs: The tape shows seven of seven majors above their 200-day simple moving averages, six of them with confirmed golden crosses (50-day above 200-day). Bitcoin is up 6.66% on the day, 12.13% on the week, 33.48% on the month. Ethereum is up 5.29% on the day, 10.73% on the week, 45.88% on the month. The momentum is directionally clean across all time horizons and all assets. Regime is unambiguous: above trend, ascending, no conflicting crosses. This is not a debate.

Momentum indicators across the board confirm the move without divergence. Bitcoin RSI sits at 73.8, Ethereum at 72.4, Solana at 70.6, BNB at 72.8, Doge at 71.7. All are above 70 and all have MACD above signal line. In a typical setup, RSI above 70 signals overbought conditions; here, the 200-day golden cross across the board suggests the uptrend is structural rather than tactical. The risk is not that momentum is broken but that it is compressed. Seven of seven assets elevated in RSI with seven of seven in uptrend creates a narrow field: if one cracks, the crowding makes a cascade more likely than an orderly unwind.

Funding costs reveal the machine at work. Bitcoin and Solana fund at 0.01% per 8-hour interval, annualizing to 11.0%, while Ethereum sits at 0.0021% annualizing to 2.3%. This spread matters: Bitcoin longs are expensive to hold on leverage, Ethereum longs are cheap. Open interest in Bitcoin is 2.55 billion USD, in Ethereum 1.70 billion. Both are material. The long-short ratio on Bitcoin is 0.94 (slightly more shorts than longs), while Ethereum is 1.09 and Solana has swung to 1.59 (heavily long). Solana also shows the hardest funding at 11.0% annual, meaning holders of leveraged longs are paying the most to stay in the trade. In the last 3 hours for Bitcoin, longs liquidated 335k USD and shorts 141k; Solana in the last 3 hours saw longs liquidate only 45k and shorts blow out for 382k. The machines are catching the bearish overleverage in the altcoins while Bitcoin shorts still hold.

Spot ETF flows display a window disagreement worth naming. On 21 Sep itself, Bitcoin saw an 68.1 million USD inflow and Ethereum a 65.7 million inflow. Over the last five sessions, Bitcoin faced a net 85.7 million outflow and Ethereum a net 196.0 million outflow. Same-direction days for Bitcoin stand at 3, for Ethereum at 2, confirming the reversal is real and recent rather than noise. Traditional finance is buying today but sold harder last week. Stablecoin float sits at 310.19 billion USD, up 0.65% on the month, a negligible change. Dry powder is flat, which in an uptrend means buyers are committing capital instead of holding it in reserve.

Whale flows over the last 24 hours show a net 307.6 million USD moving off exchanges, with Bitcoin accounting for 358.3 million off and Ethereum seeing 50.7 million onto exchanges. The weekly net for the week ending 21 Sep shows 229 million moving onto exchanges, reversing the prior week's off-exchange movement of 347 million. Bitcoin alone moved 358 million off exchanges in the last 24 hours, yet the week shows 229 million net onto exchanges: the spread means this offshore move is extremely recent and the weekly tally has three more days of data baked in. Looking at the biggest single moves, Coinbase Institutional saw 358 million in Bitcoin leave the platform in the last 24 hours, while Binance saw Bitcoin move onto the platform. Bitfinex shed 160 million in Tether. The flows are mixed by venue and by asset, a hallmark of accumulation taking place beneath the surface while the indices rise.

Fear and Greed sits at 70, labeled Greed, up from a 30-day range floor of 50. The crowd is in the upper half of the sentiment range. Bitcoin dominance is 58.8%, down from where it sat when altcoins began their explosive run: Doge is up 46% on the month, Solana 57%, Cardano 27%, Ripple 52%, all materially outpacing Bitcoin's 33%. The top movers today are fringe assets (Pepe up 20.16%, Tao up 19.56%), while the bottom tier shows mild losses (Pendle down 6.12%, ENA down 3.14%). The breadth is strong but the leadership is diffuse. Total market cap is 2.95 trillion USD, up 2.74% on the day. Watch for a reversion in the five-session ETF trend: if the next two or three sessions see continued inflows rather than a return to outflows, the traditional-finance buyers have broken through a ceiling. A flip in Bitcoin dominance above 60% would also signal a return to Bitcoin leadership and a narrowing of the altcoin outperformance. Funding costs in Solana and the fringe assets are the pressure valve; if they spike much higher, the longs in those names will begin to hemorrhage.
